# ADR 0034 amendment: v1 target platform and the OS seam

## Context

The operator set the shell's v1 platform scope on 2026-10-16, in session with the design seat: **v1 ships for macOS on Apple Silicon only; Windows and x64 macOS come after v1, on demand; the OS seam stays explicit in the seat launch/wake layer.** His follow-up idea, Linux inside a Docker container, is the cheapest second platform and the seed of a hosted institution. ADR 0034 §2.5.1 names three platform-native installers (macOS `dmg`, Windows `exe`, Linux `AppImage`) as the artifact class without a v1 scope line, and no decision record names where OS-specific behaviour may live. Reviewers of packaging and launch PRs during the FM v1 walk week have no rule to cite.

Facts verified on 2026-10-16 (Institution `dev` 4fd5945, Brain `dev` c9d894c6, Electron release assets):

- `harness/electron-builder.yml:54` emits one target: `zip`, `arch: arm64`; `npmRebuild: false`; the organism's dependencies are rebuilt for the bundled Electron by `pack.mjs` for the **host** architecture (one staging directory, no target-arch parameter, `@electron/rebuild` without `--arch` — @neo-gpt-sophie's source read at Institution 3ec914d, `pack.mjs:783–820`), and `runtimeGeneration.mjs:585–587` verifies the observed architecture at runtime publication, so a cross-architecture shell over host-built natives refuses itself. The single architecture is the pipeline's, not Electron's: Electron 43.5.0 publishes `darwin-x64`, `darwin-arm64`, `linux-arm64` and `linux-x64` release assets (HTTP 302 on each).
- Platform-specific code census: the Harness shell carries three files with macOS references (`harness/install.mjs`, `harness/main.mjs`, `harness/runtimeGeneration.mjs`; seven hits) and one `win32` mention (`harness/prepareAssets.mjs`). The Brain's seat launch and wake layer carries the rest (`ai/daemons/wake/daemon.mjs` 37, `ai/scripts/diagnostics/dialogGateRig.mjs` 21, `ai/scripts/lifecycle/resumeHarness.mjs` 19, `ai/daemons/wake/localWakeAdapters.mjs` 13, `ai/daemons/wake/buildReceiverManifest.mjs` 9, `ai/services/fleet/deriveHarnessLaunchSpec.mjs` 4, four more files under five), with a `tmux` adapter for non-`darwin` hosts (`ai/scripts/lifecycle/resumeHarness.mjs:218`) and `win32` paths in several files, but no Linux-specific adapter (corrected 2026-10-16 after review 5550007805). `deriveHarnessLaunchSpec.mjs` already keys on harness kind (`antigravity`, `claude-code`, `claude-desktop`, `codex`, `codex-desktop`); the OS axis does not exist yet.

Sweeps — Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open neo issues at 2026-10-16T15:09:55Z; no equivalent (adjacent: #19382 ADR-0034 §2.3 item 10; #19729 / #19730 ADR custody; #15243 the web layer's headed three-OS tear-out matrix). A2A in-flight claims, last 60 min: none on platform scope. Memory Core rationale sweep (`query_raw_memories` on the problem's nouns): no prior platform-scope decision; the runtime-generation and harness-kind memories confirm the launch layer's shape. Own-assignment sweep: #15243 is the same OS axis on a different surface (headed browsers, not the packaged shell) and stays as is. Structure-map gate: N/A — the change amends an existing ADR file in place; no new file or directory.

## The Problem

Three gaps, one record. (1) §2.5.1 reads as if three installers ship together; v1 ships one, and the order after v1 is undecided on paper. (2) The OS seam the operator asked for exists de facto in the Brain's launch/wake layer but is named nowhere, so the walk-week fixes can leak `darwin` assumptions into the shell or into fleet services outside that layer without a reviewer being able to cite a rule. (3) The first cheap second platform — Linux arm64 in a container: same architecture, the plane already runs as Linux containers, CI has arm64 Linux runners, CLI harnesses exist on Linux, no Claude Desktop — is an idea in a chat, not a recorded next step.

## The Architectural Reality

ADR 0034 governs the shell (`harness/`, shipped from the Institution) and its bootstrap of the plane (Brain). §2.5 Distribution: item 1 artifacts, item 2 signing as a release-line concern, items 3–4 update cadence; §2.6's falsifier already bans `process.versions.electron` branches inside `src/` and `apps/`, so platform awareness has named homes by precedent. The seat launch and wake layer is Brain substrate: `ai/services/fleet/deriveHarnessLaunchSpec.mjs` (harness-kind launch specs), `ai/daemons/wake/*` (receiver manifest, local wake adapters, the wake daemon), `ai/scripts/lifecycle/resumeHarness.mjs`. The previous two amendments to this ADR (ADR 0038 §3.3, 2026-08-08; the runtime-continuity amendment, 2026-10-13, #19725) set the convention: a header-table row plus an in-place `### §2.x Amendment — <title> (date, #N)` section with provenance brackets.

## The Fix

One PR in `neomjs/neo`, `learn/agentos/decisions/0034-electron-shell-architecture.md`:

1. A header-table row `**Platform amendment**` (2026-10-16, this ticket) summarising the scope.
2. A new section `### §2.7 Amendment — Target platforms for v1 and the OS seam (2026-10-16, #N)` before `## 3. Consequences`, stating: **(a)** v1 ships one artifact, macOS on Apple Silicon; the §2.5.1 artifact class stays the end state. **(b)** The post-v1 order and each step's trigger: Linux arm64 in a Docker container first (CI-reachable; the hosted-institution seed), x64 macOS when a concrete machine needs it, Windows on the first outside team that runs it — each its own packaging leaf with a native smoke on the target and an artifact receipt, never a config-flag toggle, because the pipeline rebuilds for the host architecture. **(c)** The OS seam: the shell carries no platform branches beyond the three files named above; OS-specific seat launch and wake behaviour lives in the Brain's launch/wake layer, keyed by harness kind and platform; the first non-macOS leaf makes the seam explicit (one adapter per harness kind × platform) and carries the platform-branch census as its first deliverable. **(d)** The falsifier: a new `process.platform` / `darwin` / `win32` branch in the shell outside those files, or in a Brain fleet service outside that layer, violates this section on its face. **(e)** Identity portability: no walk or platform leaf moves a peer; a cold first run is a fresh institution; a seat move's minimum is the seat's harness-local memory, its credential and its seat definition, and the shared record stays with the plane (Brain #571's lane).
3. A one-line pointer from §2.5.1 to §2.7.

No code, no build target, no Institution or Brain change in this PR.

## Contract Ledger Matrix

N/A — no runtime, config or tool surface changes; the consumed surface is the decision record itself, read by PR reviewers.

## Decision Record impact

`amends` ADR 0034 (§2.5.1's scope for v1; new §2.7). No Discussion: the scope call is the operator's (a product boundary, Tier 4) and the seam rule is design-seat substrate; the challenge path is this PR's cross-family review. Not `supersedes`: §2.5's artifact class, signing and update decisions stand.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] ADR 0034 carries the `**Platform amendment**` header row and `§2.7` with items (a)–(e), each fact cited with repo, path and SHA as verified on 2026-10-16.
- [ ] §2.5.1 points to §2.7 in one line; no other section's text changes.
- [ ] The amendment names the three shell files and the Brain layer paths that may carry platform branches today, and states the falsifier.
- [ ] The PR is reviewed cross-family and merged to `dev` by the operator.

## Out of Scope

Any build-target change (`electron-builder.yml`, `pack.mjs`); a Linux or x64 adapter; Windows signing; the Intel plane; the seat-move/export design (Brain #571); the web layer's three-OS matrix (#15243).

## Avoided Traps

- A new ADR: the shell already has its record; a fourth decision file for one scope line would split the shell's authority.
- Reading `@electron/universal` in the lockfile or the installer's `mac` / `mac-arm64` glob as a dual-architecture payload: transitive and permissive, not evidence.
- Promising Windows for v1 because §2.5.1 lists an `exe`: the artifact class is the end state, not the v1 scope.
